newsitem.title: USA: Northwest delays Wash. gas plant outage.
newsitem.headline: Northwest delays Wash. gas plant outage.

text.p: Northwest Pipeline Co delayed the maintenance outage of a natural gas processing plant in western Washington to Oct 1 from Sunday Sept 15, the company said Friday.
"It has been rescheduled to Oct 1," said spokeswoman Susan Flaim, adding the outage of the 690 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) Sumner plant would last until Dec 15 after the change.
"It's not uncommon to reschedule. It was nothing out of the ordinary," she said.
The outage was planned to shore up the plant's foundation, and expected to reduce its throughput by 70 mmcfd, she said.
She said Northwest had notified customers of the postponement Aug 29, adding the Sumner outage would have little impact on supply to customers.
Northwest's gas thoughput systemwide is 2.4 billion cubic feet a day.
Based in Salt Lake City, Utah, Northwest is a subsidiary of William Cos Inc, and operates 4,000 miles of pipeline in seven western states.
